senses.gloss:
श्वि श्वि (this rt. assumes the form शु,
q. v., in some of its tenses and derivatives;
cf. rt. शव्), cl. 1. P. श्वयति, शुशाव or शिश्वाय
(2nd sing. शुशविथ or शिश्वयिथ, 3rd du. शुशु-
वतुस् or शिश्वियतुस्), श्वयिष्यति, अश्वयीत् or
अश्वत् or अशिश्वियत्, Prec. शूयात्, श्वयितुम्, to
swell, increase, grow; to thrive; to appear (Ved.,
see वि-श्वि, referred by some to rt. श्वित्); to go, ap-
proach: Pass. शूयते, Aor. अश्वायि: Caus. श्वाय-
यति, -यितुम्, Aor. अशूशवत् or अशिश्वयत्, (accord-
ing to others also अशीशवत्): Desid. of Caus. शुशा-
वयिषति or शिश्वाययिषति, to cause to swell or
[]
grow or be prosperous: Desid. शिश्वयिषति: Intens.
शेश्वीयते, शोशूयते, शेश्वयीति, शेश्वेति, to swell
much; [cf. Gr. κυ-έ-ω, κύ-ος, κῦ-μα, κύ-η-μα,
κύ-αρ, κύ-τ-ος, κοῖ-λο-ς, κοιλ-ία, καυλό-ς, κύ-λο-ν,
ἐγ-κισσάω, κίσσα, κύαμος, κύαθος, κῶνος, κηκίς,
κίκυς, (probably also) κίων, κίω, κινέω, perhaps also
κό-μη (for κύ-μη): Lat. in-ci-ens, cu-mu-lu-s,
cavu-s, cau-li-s, cau-lœ, cœlu-m, ciliu-m, super-
cili-um, cuneus, crescere; coma: Goth. us-hul-
on, hul-undi: Old Germ. hol, (according to some)
wī-t, ‘wide’ (= श्वित): Angl. Sax. hol: Hib. cin-
neas, cinneachdin, ‘growth, increase.’]

श्विक्न श्विक्न, आस्, m. pl., N. of a race; [cf.
श्वैक्न.]

श्वित् श्वित् (perhaps a kind of Nom.
based on a lost rt. श्वि, cf. Zend śpi-
तम, &c.), cl. 1. A. श्वेतते (Ved. also P. -ति),
शिश्विते, श्वेतिष्यते, अश्वेतिष्ट, अश्वितत्, श्वेतितुम्,
to be or become white, (according to Vopa-deva
XXI. 15. श्वेतयति = श्वेताश्वम् आचष्टे); [cf.
Lith. swe†ciu for swetiu, ‘I shine;’ Inf. swe†sti for
swe†t-ti, (perhaps also) swe†ta-s, ‘the world;’ kaiciu
for kaitiu, kaitinu, ‘I make hot;’ kais-tu for
kait-tu, ‘I become warm;’ kaitau: Slav. svit-a-ti,
‘to become light;’ swjet, ‘light, the world.’]

स्वित् स्वित् or स्विद्, ind. a particle of inter-
rogation or inquiry (often implying doubt or surprise,
and translateable by ‘hey?’ ‘what?’ ‘can it be that?’);
an expletive (often redundant, but sometimes per-
haps used disjunctively, and equivalent to ‘either,’
‘or’).

श्वित, अस्, आ, अम्, white; (अम्), n. whiteness
(according to Sāy.).
श्वित्त, अस्, आ, अम्, see Pāṇ. VII. 2, 16, 17.

श्वितान, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. being white, white-
coloured, (Sāy. = श्वेतमान, श्वेत-वर्ण, Ṛg-
veda VI. 6, 2.)

श्विति, whiteness, a white colour (according to
Sāy.).
—श्वित्य्-अञ्च्, अङ्, -तीची, अक्, Ved. going to
whiteness, becoming white, white-coloured, fair-com-
plexioned, white, (Sāy. on Ṛg-veda VII. 83, 8.
श्वित्यञ्चः = श्वितं श्वैत्यं नैर्मल्यम् अञ्-
चन्तो गच्छन्तः.)

श्वित्न, white (according to Sāy. on Ṛg-veda I.
100, 18).

श्वित्न्य, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. white, white-coloured,
fair-complexioned (said of the winds or Maruts ac-
cording to Sāy. on Ṛg-veda I. 100, 18; but accord-
ing to some more probably referring to the fair-
coloured worshippers of Indra as opposed to the
darker aborigines of India).
श्वित्य, अस्, आ, अम्, white, white-coloured.

श्वित्र, अम्, n. morbid whiteness of the skin,
white leprosy, vitiligo; = अन्तरिक्ष (Ved., cf.
श्वैत्रेय); (आ), f. a proper N.
—श्वित्र-घ्नी, f.
‘removing whiteness of the skin,’ the plant Tragia
Involucrata (= पीत-पर्णी).

श्वित्रिन्, ई, इणी, इ, affected with whiteness of the
skin or leprosy, leprous; (ई), m. a leper.
श्वित्र्य, अस्, m., Ved. a son of Śvitrā.

श्विन्द् श्विन्द् (connected with rt. श्वित्),
cl. 1. A. श्विन्दते, शिश्विन्दे, श्विन्दिष्-
यते, श्विन्दितुम्, to be white, become white; to be
cold (according to some); [cf. probably Gr. κυδνός,
κυδρός, κῦδος; Goth. hveits, hvaitei; Old Germ.
hwiz, hwaizi, hiza, haiz; Angl. Sax. hvit, hvœte.]
स्विका, f. See under स्वक, col. 1.
स्विन् in शत-स्विन्, q. v.

स्वी-करण, अम्, n. making one's own, appropria-
tion, adopting, taking, accepting, assenting, agreeing,
assent, promise.
—स्वीकरण-कर्मन्, आ, आ, अ, Ved.
whose function is to appropriate.

स्वीकरण स्वी-करण, स्वी-कृत, स्वीय, &c.
See p. 1158, col. 3.

स्वी-करणीय, अस्, आ, अम्, to be appropriated; to
be admitted or acknowledged or accepted; to be as-
sumed; to be assented or agreed to; to be pro-
mised.

स्वी-कर्तृ, ता, त्री, तृ, one who appropriates or
accepts or admits, &c.

स्वी-कार, अम्, n. making one's own, taking on
one's self, appropriation, adopting, assuming, assump-
tion, claiming, claim; assent, agreement, consent;
promise.
—स्वीकार-रहित, अस्, आ, अम्, devoid of
assent, not agreed to.
—स्वीकारान्त (˚र-अन्˚), अस्,
आ, अम्, ended or concluded by assent; agreed to.

स्वी-कार्य, अस्, आ, अम्, to be admitted, to be as-
sumed (in argument).

स्वी-कृ, cl. 8. P. -करोति, &c., to make one's own,
own, win, appropriate, claim; to take upon one's
self; to adopt, admit, assume (in argument); to as-
sent, agree to.

स्वी-कृत, अस्, आ, अम्, appropriated, owned, ac-
cepted, admitted, acknowledged, adopted, claimed,
agreed, assented to, promised.

स्वी-कृत्य, ind. having agreed to or promised;
having satisfied.

स्वीय, अस्, आ, अम्, own, relating or belonging to
one's self, peculiar, characteristic; (आ), f. one's own
wife, a faithful wife, one solely attached to her own
husband; [cf. Gr. ἑός, αφέος, σφός.]
—स्वीयाक्षर
(˚य-अक्˚), अस्, m. one's own handwriting or signa-
ture, autograph, (Śabda-k.)

स्विद् स्विद्, cl. 4. P. स्विद्यति, सिष्वेद,
स्वेत्स्यति, अस्विदत्, स्वेत्तुम्, to sweat,
perspire; cl. 1. A. स्वेदते, सिष्विदे, स्वेदितुम्, to
be anointed; to be greasy or unctuous; to pour forth,
shed (?) ; to be disturbed: Caus. स्वेदयति, -यितुम्,
Aor. असिस्विदत्, to cause to sweat; to make warm,
heat: Desid. of Caus. सिस्वेदयिषति: Desid. सि-
ष्वित्सति: Intens. सेष्विद्यते, सेष्वेत्ति; [cf. Gr.
ἱδ-ί-ω, ἷδος, ἱδ-ρό-ς, ἱδ-ρώ(τ)-ς, σίδηρος; Lat. sud-
ā-re, sud-or, sud-ariu-m; Old Norse sveit-i; Old
Germ. sveiz; Goth. sveitan; Angl. Sax. swœtan;
Eng. sweat.]

स्विदित, अस्, आ, अम्, sweated, melted; sweating,
perspiring.

स्विन्न, अस्, आ, अम्, perspired, sweated, covered
with perspiration, perspiring; steeped.
—स्विन्नाङ्-
गुलि (˚न-अङ्˚), इस्, इस्, इ, having perspiring or moist
fingers.
स्विष्ट स्व्-इष्ट, स्विष्ट-कृत्. See p. 1126.
